short: A statutory retirement saving with employer and employee contributions.
seoTitle: Provident Fund — Meaning, Formula and Example
metaDescription: A statutory retirement saving with employer and employee contributions. It also represents a real cost in CTC and a real deduction from take-home pay.
definition: The Employees' Provident Fund is a statutory retirement scheme where both employee and employer contribute a percentage of basic pay plus dearness allowance each month, and the accumulated balance earns interest.
bodyHtml:
Why Provident Fund matters

PF is a legal obligation once thresholds are met, and it is one of the most closely enforced. It also represents a real cost in CTC and a real deduction from take-home pay.

Provident Fund formula

Employee contribution = 12% of basic plus DA

The employer contributes an equal amount, part of which is directed to the pension scheme.

How Provident Fund works in practice

Deposit within the monthly deadline and file the return; delays attract interest and damages. Employees can track their balance against their universal account number, which follows them across jobs.

faq.question: Is PF mandatory for all businesses?
faq.answer: It applies once the establishment crosses the prescribed employee threshold, with voluntary coverage possible below it.

faq.question: Can an employee opt out of PF?
faq.answer: Only in limited cases, typically where salary at joining exceeds the wage ceiling and there is no existing PF membership.
